name: search
description: Search Slack messages, files, channels, and users visible to the authorized principal. Prefer search_messages when only messages are needed.

query.description: What to look for, in plain words. Slack's own search operators work too, for example `in:#design`, `from:@dana`, `has:link`, and `"a quoted phrase"`. A query nothing matches comes back as an empty result rather than an error, so widen the words before concluding the workspace has nothing.

limit.description: Maximum results to return across all four kinds. Defaults to 20.

cursor.description: Send `null` for the first page. To continue an earlier call, pass back the exact `next_cursor` string a previous call to this tool returned, with that call's other arguments unchanged. It is an opaque cursor: a long provider-generated string, not a page number, an offset, or an index. Never construct, guess, shorten, or increment this token; when you have no token from a previous call, the value is `null`. A result whose `next_cursor` is `null` is the last page: stop there rather than calling again.

name: search_messages
description: Search Slack messages relevant to a query. Workspace-bot search is limited by Slack to a user-initiated event and public-channel access.

query.description: What to look for in message text, in plain words. Narrow to one conversation or one author with `channel_id` and `author_user_id` rather than writing `in:` or `from:` operators here.

channel_id.description: Return only messages posted in one conversation. It is a Slack conversation id, such as `C0123ABCDEF` for a public channel, `G0123ABCDEF` for a private channel or group message, or `D0123ABCDEF` for a direct message; get one from find_channels. A channel name such as `#design` is not an id and is refused. Omit it, or send `null`, to search every conversation the credential can see. A well-formed id for a conversation the credential cannot see is not refused — it returns no matches rather than an error.

author_user_id.description: Return only messages written by one person. It is a Slack user id such as `U0123ABCDEF`; get one from find_users, and a display name or email address is not one. Omit it, or send `null`, for any author. A well-formed id for the wrong person is not refused — it returns no matches rather than an error.

after.description: Return only messages posted after this Unix time, in whole seconds — the part of a message `ts` before the dot, so `1767225600` is 2026-01-01. Omit it, or send `null`, for no lower bound. Milliseconds are a date tens of thousands of years out, which matches nothing and reads as an empty result.

before.description: Return only messages posted before this Unix time, in whole seconds — the part of a message `ts` before the dot, so `1767225600` is 2026-01-01. Omit it, or send `null`, for no upper bound. Milliseconds are a date tens of thousands of years out, so every message is before it and the bound does nothing.

sort.description: Order matches by `score`, which is Slack's relevance ranking, or by `timestamp`, which is when they were posted. Defaults to `score`.

sort_dir.description: `desc` puts the best-ranked or most recent match first, `asc` the reverse. Defaults to `desc`.

include_bots.description: Include messages posted by bots and apps. Defaults to false, which returns only what people wrote.

limit.description: Maximum messages to return. Defaults to 20.

cursor.description: Send `null` for the first page. To continue an earlier call, pass back the exact `next_cursor` string a previous call to this tool returned, with that call's other arguments unchanged. It is an opaque cursor: a long provider-generated string, not a page number, an offset, or an index. Never construct, guess, shorten, or increment this token; when you have no token from a previous call, the value is `null`. A result whose `next_cursor` is `null` is the last page: stop there rather than calling again.

name: find_users
description: Find Slack users by name, display name, real name, email address, or user ID.

query.description: Part of a name, display name, real name, email address, or user id to match, for example `Dana`, `dana@example.com`, or `U0123ABCDEF`. Matching is case-insensitive and on the stored profile only, so a nickname nobody has typed into Slack finds no one rather than failing.

include_deleted.description: Include deactivated accounts. Defaults to false.

limit.description: Maximum users to return. Defaults to 50.

name: find_channels
description: Find Slack conversations by name or conversation ID within the authorized credential's visibility.

query.description: Part of a conversation name or a conversation id to match, for example `design` or `C0123ABCDEF`. Match it against the name as Slack stores it, without the leading `#`. Only conversations the credential can already see are searched, so a private channel it was never invited to is absent rather than refused.

include_archived.description: Include archived conversations. Defaults to false.

limit.description: Maximum conversations to return. Defaults to 50.

name: read_message_context
description: Read a bounded window around one Slack message timestamp.

channel_id.description: The conversation the message is in. It is a Slack conversation id, such as `C0123ABCDEF` for a public channel, `G0123ABCDEF` for a private channel or group message, or `D0123ABCDEF` for a direct message; get one from find_channels. A channel name such as `#design` is not an id and is refused.

message_ts.description: The message to center the window on. Copy Slack's `ts` value exactly as a returned message carries it, for example `1735689600.123456`; it is an id, not a date. Trimming its digits or converting it to a date names no message, which reads as an empty result rather than an error.

before.description: How many messages posted before the target one to include. Defaults to 10; 0 returns none.

after.description: How many messages posted after the target one to include. Defaults to 5; 0 returns none.

name: read_channel
description: Read messages from a Slack conversation.

channel_id.description: The conversation to read. It is a Slack conversation id, such as `C0123ABCDEF` for a public channel, `G0123ABCDEF` for a private channel or group message, or `D0123ABCDEF` for a direct message; get one from find_channels. A channel name such as `#design` is not an id and is refused.

limit.description: Maximum messages to return, newest first. Defaults to 50.

cursor.description: Send `null` for the first page. To continue an earlier call, pass back the exact `next_cursor` string a previous call to this tool returned, with that call's other arguments unchanged. It is an opaque cursor: a long provider-generated string, not a page number, an offset, or an index. Never construct, guess, shorten, or increment this token; when you have no token from a previous call, the value is `null`. A result whose `next_cursor` is `null` is the last page: stop there rather than calling again.

channel_id.description: The conversation the thread is in. It is a Slack conversation id, such as `C0123ABCDEF` for a public channel, `G0123ABCDEF` for a private channel or group message, or `D0123ABCDEF` for a direct message; get one from find_channels. A channel name such as `#design` is not an id and is refused.

thread_ts.description: The thread's parent message, which is the `thread_ts` a reply carries, or the `ts` of the message the thread hangs off. Copy Slack's `ts` value exactly as a returned message carries it, for example `1735689600.123456`; it is an id, not a date. Trimming its digits or converting it to a date names no message, which reads as an empty result rather than an error.

limit.description: Maximum messages to return, including the parent. Defaults to 100.

cursor.description: Send `null` for the first page. To continue an earlier call, pass back the exact `next_cursor` string a previous call to this tool returned, with that call's other arguments unchanged. It is an opaque cursor: a long provider-generated string, not a page number, an offset, or an index. Never construct, guess, shorten, or increment this token; when you have no token from a previous call, the value is `null`. A result whose `next_cursor` is `null` is the last page: stop there rather than calling again.

name: read_file
description: Read metadata and bounded textual content for a Slack file.

file_id.description: The Slack file id, such as `F0123ABCDEF`. Messages that share a file carry it in their `files` entries; it is not a filename or a download URL.

name: send_message
description: Send a Slack message as the connected user or installed workspace bot.

channel_id.description: Where to post the message. It is a Slack conversation id, such as `C0123ABCDEF` for a public channel, `G0123ABCDEF` for a private channel or group message, or `D0123ABCDEF` for a direct message; get one from find_channels. A channel name such as `#design` is not an id and is refused.

text.description: The message body, in Slack's mrkdwn: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `<https://example.com|a link>`, `<@U0123ABCDEF>` to mention a person, and `<#C0123ABCDEF>` to link a channel. A bare `@dana` posts the literal text and notifies no one.

thread_ts.description: Post as a reply inside an existing thread, as that thread's parent `ts` copied exactly, for example `1735689600.123456`. Omit it, or send `null`, to post a new top-level message in the conversation.

name: create_conversation
description: Create a Slack channel or open a direct or group message as the connected user or installed workspace bot. Provide exactly one: `name` for a channel, or `user_ids` for a direct or group message.

name.description: Channel name without `#`, using lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores, for example `launch-oct`. Omit it when using `user_ids`.

user_ids.description: One to eight Slack user IDs from `find_users`, for example `["U0123ABCDEF"]`. One ID opens a direct message; multiple IDs open a group message. Omit it when using `name`.

is_private.description: Whether a channel created with `name` is private. Defaults to false and is ignored for direct and group messages. Channel privacy cannot be changed later through these tools.

name: add_reaction
description: Add an emoji reaction to a Slack message as the connected user or installed workspace bot.

channel_id.description: The conversation holding the message to react to. It is a Slack conversation id, such as `C0123ABCDEF` for a public channel, `G0123ABCDEF` for a private channel or group message, or `D0123ABCDEF` for a direct message; get one from find_channels. A channel name such as `#design` is not an id and is refused.

timestamp.description: The message to react to. Copy Slack's `ts` value exactly as a returned message carries it, for example `1735689600.123456`; it is an id, not a date. Trimming its digits or converting it to a date names no message, which reads as an empty result rather than an error.

name.description: The emoji's Slack name without the surrounding colons, for example `white_check_mark` or `tada`. A literal `✅`, or a name this workspace has no emoji for, is refused.

user_id.description: The Slack user id, such as `U0123ABCDEF`; get one from find_users. A display name or email address is not an id and is refused.

name: list_channel_members
description: List members of a Slack conversation.

channel_id.description: The conversation whose members to list. It is a Slack conversation id, such as `C0123ABCDEF` for a public channel, `G0123ABCDEF` for a private channel or group message, or `D0123ABCDEF` for a direct message; get one from find_channels. A channel name such as `#design` is not an id and is refused.

limit.description: Maximum member ids to return in one page. Defaults to 200.

cursor.description: Send `null` for the first page.
